recommendation: Use witness0.2.0 for W5a/W2 landing identity and global state comparison. Synthetic sensitivity passes. Hardware count/overflow/exact-correction acceptance and saved-state completeness remain separate.
application_output: Identical OK output for every new divergent control. All precise-landing failures remain first-class divergences.
fresh_reruns: Each control executes fresh subprocesses, then regenerates both sides from seed42 and pinned original inputs with detail3..6. No previous execution log is an execution input. Reproduced original chains and exact field bytes.
count_validity_controls: Reject precise boundaries with Unavailable count, missing valid value, mismatched source/profile, or Unaccounted overflow. Require complete declared CPU inventory and consistent RIP/RCX/RSI/RDI/RFLAGS. Reject an inventory CPU missing RIP/RFLAGS. This validates adapter declarations, not physical-counter truth or complete architectural capture.
limitations: No measured real KVM/perf count source, overflow or debugger exact landing acceptance
No real correction transparency or preservation of DR6/interrupt/exception state acceptance
No real guest Linux capture, actual KVM dirty-log/host-DMA integration or broad clock/entropy closure
CPU inventory and core-register consistency checks cannot detect a consistently omitted machine or architecture field
No general complete snapshot/restore, pinned-image policy or cross-host profile acceptance
Opaque or unavailable backend state must remain declared; W1 explicit protocol/state migration is not validated here
No per-instruction equivalence or representative VM/RAM/performance acceptance
Dirty omission still localizes to first audit checkpoint unless fresh full-every-boundary rerun is performed
next_gate: W5a real exact-stop hardware result, then W2 completed-boundary capture with declared CPU/count profile and W1 explicit world/control protocol state. Snapshot restore is sequenced afterward.
